mappings.note: Practical case study on warming ethanol with alkaline KMnO4 - every sub-question is about the oxidation of ethanol to ethanoic acid and the reagent's behaviour, which is LO-8.

Esterification practical: relative acid strength of ethanoic acid against HCl, the meaning of glacial acetic acid, and naming the reaction. All three are ethanoic-acid properties and esterification, LO-8.
Oil-and-water test tubes with and without soap - emulsification of the oil into micelles, which is the cleansing action of LO-9.
Soap with distilled versus hard water, foam and curdy precipitate. Hard-water failure of soap, LO-9.
Soap against detergent in the same hard water, including which pollutes - the soap/detergent distinction of LO-9 end to end.

Four sub-questions, three codes: draw the straight and branched C4 structures (C 1.3-LO-4), define catenation (LO-3), define functional group (C 1.1-LO-4). The 'what are saturated hydrocarbons' part rides with LO-3's bonding content.
Homologous-series case study: functional group, general formula and series membership (C 1.1-LO-4), plus the structure of the first alcohol (C 1.3-LO-4).
Ethanol case study - dehydration, the sodium reaction and denatured alcohol (LO-8), with an explicit demand for the structural formula (C 1.3-LO-4).
Carboxylic acid case study: the bicarbonate equation, neutralising a bee sting and the definition of esterification (LO-8), plus the electron dot structure of ethanoic acid (C 1.3-LO-4).

Three sub-questions on hard water, micelles and the soap-versus-detergent advantage (LO-9), plus one naming saponification as the commercial process (LO-8) - the same manufacture/behaviour split used across the soap family.

Table case study with three distinct demands: the electron dot structure of methanol (C 1.3-LO-4), reasoning from functional group to which compound lacks -OH (C 1.1-LO-4), and which compound effervesces with baking soda (LO-8).
Reagent-table case study: three sub-questions are ethanol and ethanoic acid reactions (LO-8); the first, why ethene decolourises bromine, is an addition reaction with no outcome (C 1.3).

Isomers of butane and the ethyne structure (C 1.3-LO-4), boiling-point order along the alkane series (C 1.1-LO-4), and which hydrocarbons undergo hydrogenation (C 1.3). The covalent-bond count rides on the ethyne structure.
Four printed ethanol reactions: knowing that alcohols do not react with NaOH and naming sodium ethoxide is LO-8; classifying one as displacement and another as oxidation is reaction-type work, C 1.3.
Covalent-bonding case study: sharing of electrons and bond types (C 1.1, no outcome covers them), carbon bonding to carbon (LO-3, catenation), and the definition of isomers (C 1.3-LO-4).

General-formula table: next homologue, formulae of butane and hexene, and identifying propyne. Every sub-question is homologous-series membership, so one code - the table's reaction-type column is never questioned.

Allotrope case study that, unlike the bare recall items mapped to CG 1, reasons explicitly from each carbon being bonded to four others and from all four valencies being satisfied - that is LO-3. The conduction contrast between diamond and graphite takes C 1.1.
Melting/boiling point table read as a homologous series: membership by general formula and the gradation of physical properties with molecular mass - both halves of LO-4.
Three demands: draw propyne from CnH2n-2 (C 1.3-LO-4), name the hydrogenation reaction and its nickel catalyst (C 1.3), and sort four formulae into alkenes and alkynes (C 1.1-LO-4).
